claims.text: The driver's own trace fails the arrival test. For this STANDARD pickup the arrival radius is 50 m, and across 93 fixes at 100% coverage the trace reports 0 qualifying in-radius fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds. Under POL-NS-02, where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the 08:20:30 cancellation, the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the $4.00 fee.

POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four conditions hold. Limb (a) is met on its face (an 'arrived' event at 08:12:35) and limb (d) is met in form (driver-cancelled at 08:20:30 with cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT, one of the three codes that limb recognises). But limb (b) fails for want of any qualifying in-radius fix, and limb (c) fails because the continuous in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum. Two of the four required conditions are unsatisfied, so nothing is chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the refund falls to be decided under POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 or POL-NS-06.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds, far short of the 300-second minimum for the STANDARD zone class. POL-NS-06 is explicit that where the dwell is shorter than the minimum the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. On this record the rider's own conduct is irrelevant to chargeability, and the clause is decisive on its own.

There is no route to accumulation under POL-NS-06(i). The derived arrival block reports 0 in-geofence runs (run_count 0, longest_run_sec 0), so there are no separate intervals to sum in the first place. In any event EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING: I disclose that it carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its absence is itself citable — no advisory covers the Raffles Place kerbside in this window, so limb (i)'s precondition of a present and populated KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT advisory cannot be met. The shortfall therefore stands unaccumulated and the full refund is undisturbed.

The 08:12:35 'arrived' marker is uncorroborated: across 93 driver fixes at 100% coverage there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip (qualifying_fix_count 0, dwell_start_offset_sec null). Under POL-NS-05(ii), where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list. The trace as a whole is also not the signature of a car held at a kerb: the driver's track runs out to 1082 m from the pin, with recorded distinct speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h, against a mean distance of 294 m.

Even on the alternative footing of POL-NS-03 the fee does not stand. POL-NS-03 refunds the rider in full where the driver held position outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, and the trace reports no qualifying stationary hold at all — mean distance from the pickup pin 294 m, maximum 1082 m, recorded speeds reaching 43.5 km/h, and zero qualifying in-geofence intervals. Whichever of POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-03 governs, the $4.00 is not left with the platform.

The driver's suggestion that the rider may have been 'looking at the wrong side' is not established on this record. Both the pickup and the dropoff carry venue_id null, so under POL-NS-03 no venue match or mismatch can be corroborated and the point is simply not established either way, leaving the distance test to govern alone. registered_pickup_points is also 1, so the pin-ambiguity route in POL-NS-03(ii) is unavailable on its own terms — and it would in any case be a platform-funded payment to the driver, never a charge retained from the rider.

The rider's own track is consistent with her account: 60 fixes between 08:08:00 and 08:22:00, every one at zero speed, every one within 40.4 m of the pickup pin, against a STANDARD rider-presence radius of 100 m. I disclose that these fixes do not pass the 25 m accuracy filter (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0), so under POL-NS-02 they count as evidence of neither presence nor absence; the point is that nothing on the driver's side places the rider anywhere else, and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee regardless.

No POL-NS-09 limb is engaged, so this case should be decided on the money rather than held. The counterparty counters are 0 and 0, so limb (c) is out; no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on 2 terminations across 132 completed trips, so limb (d) is out; and the deciding artifact is COMPLETE with 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0, 93 fixes and a rider track present, so POL-NS-08(a) to (d) — clock skew, trace defect, chat defect, fare defect — is not engaged and limb (e) is out. The fare line itself reconciles: the $4.00 charged is the greater of the STANDARD zone fee and the RYDE_X tier fee, both $4.00, so the rider's challenge is to chargeability and not to arithmetic.

claims.text: The trip record satisfies POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) on the platform's own data: it carries a driver 'arrived' event at 08:12:35, it records termination by the driver at 08:20:30 with cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT - one of the three codes limb (d) recognises - it records no boarding event, and its status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER. This is therefore not a DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission, and the only limbs still open are the geofence and dwell limbs (b) and (c).

The record's own timeline is consistent with the driver's account rather than against it. The interval from the arrival marker at 08:12:35 to cancellation at 08:20:30 is 7 minutes 55 seconds (wait_time_min 7.9), and the interval from acceptance at 08:05:10 to cancellation is 15 minutes 20 seconds. The driver says he was at the kerb for nearly eight minutes; that is exactly what the trip record measures between the marker and the cancellation. I do not contend the marker starts the dwell clock - POL-NS-01(c) fixes that at the first qualifying in-geofence fix - only that the record does not contradict the driver's account of a genuine wait.

POL-NS-04 cannot be run against the driver. The rider's locating message MSG-00212-002 was sent at 08:15:02 and the driver replied in MSG-00212-003 at 08:15:30 - 28 seconds later - so limb (b) of POL-NS-04 fails on its own terms: the driver did reply within 120 seconds, and that is so whatever the reply said. The rider's exoneration route is closed, no driver in-app call was needed, and any residual mislocation falls to be decided under POL-NS-03 rather than POL-NS-04.

The driver supplied the rider with precisely the information that resolves a kerbside pick-up: colour, model, plate SLZ9931H and position ('at the kerb outside exit A', MSG-00212-003 sent 08:15:30), and the chat record shows the rider read that message at 08:15:44. She then sent nothing further for the next four and a half minutes while the driver held the kerb, and he cancelled only at 08:20:10-08:20:30. That sequence is the behaviour of a driver actively trying to complete the pick-up, not one who abandoned it.

The GPS trace cannot be read as placing the driver away from the pickup point. The derived track puts his closest recorded approach at 37.9 m from the pin, which is inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and it never exceeds 1082.4 m from the pin across the whole waiting window, so the driver did not leave the vicinity of Raffles Place. The arrival block returns a qualifying_fix_count of 0 for the driver only because every one of his 93 fixes falls outside the 25 m accuracy filter, and POL-NS-02 directs that fixes reporting horizontal accuracy worse than 25 m 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence'. On the driver's side the trace is silent on his position at the kerb, not adverse to it; and because the same filter zeroes the rider's 60 fixes (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0), neither party is placed at the pin on admissible fixes.

The amount itself is not defective. The fare ledger's 4.00 cancellation fee is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) under the fee schedule's resolution rule, and it shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and if the charge stands it stands at 4.00, with the ledger's computed driver compensation at 3.20 (80 percent).

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on this driver. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 132 - 1.5 percent - below both the four-termination trigger and the 0.08 ratio the clause sets, so no part of the driver's compensation is withheld on that ground. These are the only two profile fields POL-NS-07 reads, and neither shows a pattern of farming no-show fees.

If the arrival question cannot be resolved on this bundle, the case belongs in human review rather than a refund. The only artifact that speaks to the driver's position at the kerb is EV-GPS-00212, and its arrival test returns zero qualifying fixes for the driver and zero for the rider, so on admissible fixes neither party is placed at the pickup pin; the third-party account that might have broken the tie is absent, because EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING - weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING) - and no advisory covers the Raffles Place kerbside in this window. With the decisive fact carried only by a trace that is complete yet cannot be run against either party, the 0.70 floor in POL-NS-09(a) is not met, and the file also engages POL-NS-09(b) in that the trip record's arrival marker and 7.9-minute wait sit against a trace showing no in-geofence dwell at all. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal, and under POL-GEN-03 the 4.00 fee is held rather than collected or refunded while the reviewer settles the open question.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the $4.00 cancellation fee charged on TRP-00212 is refunded to the rider in full.

WHY THE FEE DOES NOT STAND. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. Limb (a) is met (the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 08:12:35) and limb (d) is met (driver-cancelled at 08:20:30 with cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT). Limb (b) and limb (c) are not met. POL-NS-02 deems the driver to have arrived only where the GPS trace contains at least 3 consecutive fixes of 25 m accuracy or better inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. The trace EV-GPS-00212 (weight 1.0; complete — 93 driver fixes, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0, no detector fired) returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds. Under POL-NS-02, the absence of any qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation means the driver is not deemed to have arrived; under POL-NS-06 the effective in-geofence dwell (0 seconds) is far short of the 300-second STANDARD minimum, and the fee is refunded whether or not the rider was present or responded. Limb (a)'s marker does not help on its own: it is a status the driver set and starts nothing, since POL-NS-01(c) measures dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix.

THE DRIVER'S ACCOUNT. Your statement that you held the kerb for nearly eight minutes is not adopted as establishing arrival. wait_time_min 7.9 measures only the interval between your own arrival marker and your cancellation, not a verified in-geofence dwell. Your closest recorded approach (37.9 m) falls inside the 50 m radius, but it is computed from fixes that do not pass POL-NS-02's 25 m accuracy filter and so are not admitted as evidence of presence (nor of absence, per that same clause). I note you replied to the rider's locating message in 28 seconds (MSG-00212-003 at 08:15:30), so POL-NS-04 correctly does not apply and the rider's contact route is closed; that affects fault allocation only, not chargeability.

WHY NO ESCALATION. Your request for human review is refused, and no POL-NS-09 limb is engaged. The trace is complete and is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d), so limb (e) does not fire; the 08:12:35 'arrived' marker is a party-set status, not a platform measurement, and does not directly contradict a trace that is silent rather than contrary, so limb (b) does not fire; disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0 and 0 and no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so limbs (c) and (d) do not fire; and my confidence (0.80) is above the 0.70 floor, so limb (a) does not fire. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00212-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed) only removes the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route, and there are 0 in-geofence runs to accumulate in any event, so it changes nothing.

AMOUNTS AND REFERRALS. The $4.00 fee is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00) — a tie resolved at $4.00 — so the fare line reconciles and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays 80% ($3.20) only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not; the anti-farming counters (2 no-show terminations across 132 completed trips, 1.5%) are clean but moot. No false-arrival referral is recorded: POL-NS-05 requires the arrival marker to be shown false — the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or more at the marker's timestamp — and the derived trace does not localise the driver at 08:12:35, so that premise is not established and POL-NS-05(ii) is not reached. Finally, the rider's own track (60 fixes, 08:08-08:22, all at zero speed, all within 40.4 m of the pin) is consistent with her account but likewise fails the 25 m filter and counts as evidence of neither presence nor absence; the refund does not depend on it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the $4.00 Raffles Place cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why the charge does not stand. POL-NS-01 lets a cancellation fee be kept only if all four conditions hold. Limbs (a) and (d) are met on the trip record (a driver 'arrived' event at 08:12:35; driver-cancelled at 08:20:30 with reason EXCESSIVE_WAIT, one of the three recognised codes, and no boarding event). Limbs (b) and (c) are not. Across 93 driver fixes at 100% coverage the trace returns zero qualifying in-radius fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds, so under POL-NS-02 - whose terms are that no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation means the driver never arrived and the rider is entitled to a full refund - limb (b) fails. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, so limb (c) fails too. POL-NS-06 independently refunds the fee in full where the effective dwell is short of the minimum, whether or not the rider was present or responded.

The driver's answer - that the zero qualifying fixes arise only because all 93 driver fixes fail the 25 m accuracy filter, so the trace is 'silent, not adverse' - does not change the result. POL-NS-02 sets the 25 m bar for itself, provides that worse fixes count as evidence of neither presence nor absence, and then states the outcome for a trace with no qualifying fix: the driver never arrived. That outcome does not depend on the filtered fixes, and the 37.9 m closest approach the driver points to is a raw distance from a fix that does not qualify. The rider's 60 fixes fail the same filter, so neither party is placed at the pin on admissible fixes; that does not assist the driver, because it is the absence of any qualifying driver fix, not the rider's position, that decides limb (b).

What else the parties argued. POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied 28 seconds after the rider's locating message, so limb (b) of that clause fails and the rider's exoneration route is closed - the refund does not rest on it. The driver's account of an eight-minute kerbside wait is measured by the trip record's marker-to-cancellation interval (wait_time_min 7.9), but POL-NS-01(c) starts the clock at the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not the marker, and there is none; the record therefore does not evidence the dwell the fee needs. POL-NS-03 gives the driver nothing: it applies to a stationary hold outside the arrival radius, there is no qualifying hold on this trace, both venue_id values are null so no venue match is established either way, and registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill payment is unavailable on its own terms. The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip (2 no-show terminations over 132 completed trips, 1.5%, below both the four-termination trigger and the 0.08 ratio), but compensation is not payable in any event because POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full; it is not. The $4.00 charged is correct as arithmetic: it is the greater of the STANDARD zone fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

The requested false-arrival referral. The rider asks that the trip be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver under POL-NS-05(ii). That limb sits behind POL-NS-05's threshold: the marker is false only where the trace, at the marker's timestamp, places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or shows him travelling at 15 km/h or more. The record fixes neither - the driver's closest recorded approach is 37.9 m from the pin, inside the 50 m radius, and no derived fact states his position or speed at 08:12:35; the distinct speeds (up to 43.5 km/h) and the 1082.4 m maximum are window-wide, not marker-time, figures. The marker is uncorroborated rather than shown false, so no referral is produced on this record.

Escalation. No POL-NS-09 limb is engaged. POL-NS-08(a)-(d) are not met: the trace has 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0, 93 fixes and a rider track; the chat log is complete and consistent with trip_record.chat_message_count of 4; and the fare reconciles. The same-rider/driver dispute counters are 0 and 0 and the anti-farming check is clean, so limbs (c) and (d) are out. The deciding facts rest on weight-1.0 artifacts (the trace and the trip record), so confidence is not below the 0.70 floor and limb (a) is out. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00212-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) removes the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route, but accumulation is moot because the trace records no in-geofence runs to sum, and its absence does not lower confidence in the refund.

No profile field outside the citable set was used; the riders' and driver's ratings, account ages, lifetime trips and cancellation rates are context only and carry no weight in this outcome.

Result: FULL_REFUND of $4.00 to the rider; no driver compensation; no referrals; confidence 0.9.

The fare line itself reconciles: the $4.00 charged is the greater of the STANDARD zone fee and the RYDE_X tier fee, both $4.00, so the rider's challenge is to chargeability and not to arithmetic.

The trip record satisfies POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) on the platform's own data: it carries a driver 'arrived' event at 08:12:35, it records termination by the driver at 08:20:30 with cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT - one of the three codes limb (d) recognises - it records no boarding event, and its status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER. This is therefore not a DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission, and the only limbs still open are the geofence and dwell limbs (b) and (c).

The record's own timeline is consistent with the driver's account rather than against it. The interval from the arrival marker at 08:12:35 to cancellation at 08:20:30 is 7 minutes 55 seconds (wait_time_min 7.9), and the interval from acceptance at 08:05:10 to cancellation is 15 minutes 20 seconds. The driver says he was at the kerb for nearly eight minutes; that is exactly what the trip record measures between the marker and the cancellation. I do not contend the marker starts the dwell clock - POL-NS-01(c) fixes that at the first qualifying in-geofence fix - only that the record does not contradict the driver's account of a genuine wait.

POL-NS-04 cannot be run against the driver. The rider's locating message MSG-00212-002 was sent at 08:15:02 and the driver replied in MSG-00212-003 at 08:15:30 - 28 seconds later - so limb (b) of POL-NS-04 fails on its own terms: the driver did reply within 120 seconds, and that is so whatever the reply said. The rider's exoneration route is closed, no driver in-app call was needed, and any residual mislocation falls to be decided under POL-NS-03 rather than POL-NS-04.

The driver supplied the rider with precisely the information that resolves a kerbside pick-up: colour, model, plate SLZ9931H and position ('at the kerb outside exit A', MSG-00212-003 sent 08:15:30), and the chat record shows the rider read that message at 08:15:44. She then sent nothing further for the next four and a half minutes while the driver held the kerb, and he cancelled only at 08:20:10-08:20:30. That sequence is the behaviour of a driver actively trying to complete the pick-up, not one who abandoned it.

The GPS trace cannot be read as placing the driver away from the pickup point. The derived track puts his closest recorded approach at 37.9 m from the pin, which is inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and it never exceeds 1082.4 m from the pin across the whole waiting window, so the driver did not leave the vicinity of Raffles Place. The arrival block returns a qualifying_fix_count of 0 for the driver only because every one of his 93 fixes falls outside the 25 m accuracy filter, and POL-NS-02 directs that fixes reporting horizontal accuracy worse than 25 m 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence'. On the driver's side the trace is silent on his position at the kerb, not adverse to it; and because the same filter zeroes the rider's 60 fixes (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0), neither party is placed at the pin on admissible fixes.

The amount itself is not defective. The fare ledger's 4.00 cancellation fee is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) under the fee schedule's resolution rule, and it shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and if the charge stands it stands at 4.00, with the ledger's computed driver compensation at 3.20 (80 percent).

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on this driver. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 132 - 1.5 percent - below both the four-termination trigger and the 0.08 ratio the clause sets, so no part of the driver's compensation is withheld on that ground. These are the only two profile fields POL-NS-07 reads, and neither shows a pattern of farming no-show fees.

If the arrival question cannot be resolved on this bundle, the case belongs in human review rather than a refund. The only artifact that speaks to the driver's position at the kerb is EV-GPS-00212, and its arrival test returns zero qualifying fixes for the driver and zero for the rider, so on admissible fixes neither party is placed at the pickup pin; the third-party account that might have broken the tie is absent, because EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING - weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING) - and no advisory covers the Raffles Place kerbside in this window. With the decisive fact carried only by a trace that is complete yet cannot be run against either party, the 0.70 floor in POL-NS-09(a) is not met, and the file also engages POL-NS-09(b) in that the trip record's arrival marker and 7.9-minute wait sit against a trace showing no in-geofence dwell at all. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal, and under POL-GEN-03 the 4.00 fee is held rather than collected or refunded while the reviewer settles the open question.
